notes: Use 2026;24(3):401-408 for the issue citation; preserve first online publication date 2025-05-10 separately. Copyright 2025 does not change the issue year.
Current tool is revised; do not silently cite or apply the older 2017 analytical cross-sectional checklist as though it were this version.

The manuscript may name the instrument as planned; no formal JBI appraisal or implemented version is claimed. Reviewers must read and freeze the exact manual/template and pilot interpretation before use.

This instrument concerns analytical cross-sectional exposure/outcome associations. It is not a universal tool for cohort studies, prevalence-only descriptions, randomized effects, fee-schedule inventories or policy documents.
The paper distinguishes study-, outcome- and result-level judgments; preserve those levels instead of reducing appraisal to a numeric paper score.
No linked erratum/retraction was returned by the bounded MEDLINE/Europe PMC metadata check; this is not proof of absence.

manuscript_wording_proposal: Formal risk-of-bias appraisal remains planned. Reviewers will select design- and result-appropriate instruments, including RoB 2 for randomized intervention effects [M-010] and the revised JBI instrument for analytical cross-sectional associations [M-011]. Exact versions and interpretation rules will be documented and piloted before appraisal; these citations do not indicate that either instrument has already been applied.
boundary_notes: These two references do not cover every included design. Cohort, qualitative, quasi-experimental, service-valuation and policy assessments still need their appropriate methods.
The current protocol specifies two independent human reviewers; this task does not amend that plan or suggest that AI agents fulfill it.
M-009 may remain general secondary workflow context, but should not stand in for primary instrument citations.
No canonical register, manuscript, protocol or eligibility decisions were edited.
